name: Worklog
statusNote: Working script with generated output and double-click launchers; metrics are static text matches and honestly labeled as such.
oneLiner: A self-contained Python tool that builds a daily work log and a styled weekly value report from git commit history across a set of repos, plus manual notes for off-git work.

components.name: worklog.py
components.desc: Scans git log --numstat per configured repo, stores results, renders the report.

components.name: worklog.json
components.desc: Persisted data — commit records plus manual notes; git is the source of truth, notes survive re-scans.

components.name: value-report.html
components.desc: The latest weekly report — self-contained, print-friendly, light equity-research theme.

components.name: launchers
components.desc: WORK REPORT.bat and ADD NOTE.bat for double-click use.

dataFlow: git log --numstat runs per configured repo.
Commits are parsed into hash, date, subject, and lines added or deleted.
Results merge into the persisted store, backfilling missed days and preserving manual notes.
Weekly aggregation renders the value report as a single HTML file.
The report opens via the browser or the .bat launchers.
Manual notes append straight to the store, bypassing git entirely.
integrations: Local git binary (hard error if missing)
Reads other repos' DECISIONS.md to count documented decisions
Scans for test-function patterns for an honestly-labeled static count
decisions: Explicitly honest about metric limits — static text matches, not runtime counts, stated plainly.
The factual record is separated from any eloquent narrative, which is deferred to a later polish pass.
Themed light, equity-research style, since it covers the finance work.
Standard library only — no dependencies to install.
